narrative.headline: Attacking Mid and Striker are clear weaknesses costing Brentford the gap to the top three.
narrative.summary: Brentford sit an estimated 3rd in the Premier League with a squad valued at EUR 584.8M, below the league average of EUR 658.6M. We score 2.0 goals per game — above the league average of 1.35 — but 14.8% below the top sides' average of 2.35, and our pass accuracy of 76.42% ranks 18th, nearly 9 points below those top sides. The clearest opportunity is addressing the Attacking Mid position (scored 30/100, our weakest area) and the Striker position (scored 38/100), where targeted signings at strong value could close that offensive gap.
title_plan: Pass accuracy at 76.42% ranks 18th — the top sides average 85.39%. This drag runs through Centre Back (16th percentile), Central Mid (19th percentile), and Attacking Mid (29th percentile), limiting our ability to control games.

Shots on target at 4.6 per game rank 10th and sit 14.2% below the top sides' average of 5.36. Our Attacking Mid produces just 0.31 shots on target per 90 (3rd percentile), the single biggest underperformance in the squad.

Our Striker scores 0.2 goals per 90 (34th percentile) against a top-sides average of 0.65. Signing a 22-year-old from the Eredivisie (market value EUR 800K, 86th percentile on key stats, 6.91 aerials won per 90) could transform that output at minimal cost.
money_plan: Five players are out of contract in 8 months, representing EUR 30.3M of value at risk. The 30-year-old central midfielder (market value EUR 10M, 15% of minutes) is the priority renewal or sale decision; the remaining four play negligible minutes and should be released.

A 21-year-old on loan (market value EUR 28M, only 9% of the minutes of our most-used player) should be sent out on a development loan to grow value — retaining a purchase option before that market value rises further.

Our realistic budget is EUR 45M per signing. The top Attacking Mid target (22-year-old from the Eredivisie, market value EUR 13M, 88th percentile) represents a EUR 63.7M saving versus what a comparable top-side player would cost, preserving budget for the Striker position.
success_plan: Priority 1 — this window: Sign the 22-year-old Attacking Mid from the Eredivisie (market value EUR 13M, 0.8 assists per 90 at 98th percentile, 3.61 successful dribbles per 90 at 98th percentile). This is the highest-impact, lowest-cost fix available.

Priority 2 — this window: Add a Striker. The 22-year-old from the Eredivisie (market value EUR 800K, 0.89 goals per 90 at 92nd percentile, 2.67 key passes per 90 at 97th percentile) offers extraordinary value; the 27-year-old from Liga Portugal (market value EUR 35M, 1.29 goals per 90 at 97th percentile) is the proven alternative if budget allows.

narrative.headline: Feyenoord lead the Eredivisie on goals and chances but a weak aerial game and below-par xG threaten title credentials.
narrative.summary: Feyenoord sit top of the Eredivisie with a squad valued at EUR 245M — three times the league average of EUR 81M — scoring 3.16 goals per game against a league average of 1.89. However, the team ranks 18th (last) in aerial duels won per game at 10.67 versus a contenders' average of 11.49, and sits 14% below the top sides in xG per game (2.35 vs 2.74), suggesting goals are coming more efficiently than the underlying chances created. The main opportunity is to strengthen centre-back with a physically dominant profile to close the aerial gap, while freeing up budget by moving on underused, high-value players.
title_plan: Aerial duels are the clearest weakness: Feyenoord win only 10.67 per game (ranked 18th in the league) versus a contenders' average of 11.49. The current centre-backs average just 1.72 aerial duels won per 90, below both the league average (2.05) and contenders' average (1.82).

xG per game (2.35) sits 14% below the top sides (2.74), meaning goals are outpacing chances created. Adding a more physically dominant centre-back who also wins headers in the attacking third — or upgrading the goalkeeper's long-ball delivery from 13.43 to near the league average of 21.47 — could unlock higher-quality chances.

The defensive midfield's long-ball output is critically low at 2.10 per 90 versus a contenders' average of 3.58 (17th percentile), limiting transitions. Pairing a cover-shadow defensive midfielder upgrade with a dominant centre-back would connect defence to attack more effectively and raise xG closer to the top-sides benchmark.
money_plan: Seven players have contracts expiring in eight months, putting EUR 19.9M of value at risk. The priority is to extend or sell the 29-year-old centre-back (market value EUR 4M, 84% of minutes played, performance score 70%) before he leaves for free — renew now or sell in January to recoup value.

Four players are underusing their market value on the bench: a 24-year-old (market value EUR 11M, only 18% of minutes) should be sold; a 19-year-old (EUR 5M, 16% of minutes) and another 19-year-old (EUR 5M, 20% of minutes) should go out on loan to grow value; a second 24-year-old (EUR 5M, 21% of minutes, contract expiring) should be sold now.

The best-value centre-back target is a 26-year-old from the Championship with a market value of just EUR 1.2M, eight months left on his contract, and a Duel Win % of 79.31 (99th percentile) versus our current 50.73 — a potential saving of EUR 9.9M versus what a top-side equivalent would cost.
success_plan: Immediate priority (this window): Sell or extend the expiring 29-year-old centre-back before value is lost. Use proceeds plus the EUR 16.5M per-signing budget to acquire the 26-year-old Championship centre-back (market value EUR 1.2M, 99th percentile Duel Win %) to fix the aerial weakness immediately.

Short-term (next 6 months): Sell the benched 24-year-old winger/midfielder (market value EUR 11M) and the expiring 24-year-old (EUR 5M) to free wage space and capital. Send both 19-year-olds (EUR 5M each) on loan to maximise development and future resale value.

12-month outlook: Address the goalkeeper's long-ball deficiency (13.43 vs league average 21.47 per 90) by targeting the 25-year-old Serie B option (market value EUR 400K, 97th percentile for long balls at 21.2 per 90) as a low-cost upgrade that keeps squad value and age profile young — 67% of minutes currently go to players 24 or under.

narrative.headline: Aris concedes 2.0 goals per game — three times the top sides' rate — and must fix defending before anything else.
narrative.summary: Aris sits estimated 13th of 14 teams, scoring 1.0 goals per game against a league average of 1.21 and a top-sides average of 2.35, while conceding 2.0 per game versus the top sides' 0.67 — the worst defensive record in the division. Attacking mid is the only position rated a outright weakness (score 35/100), with key passes at 0.65 per game against a league average of 2.03. The good news is the club's xG of 1.68 per game ranks 5th, meaning chances are being created but not converted, and attacking-mid targets are available with market values between EUR 750k and EUR 1M — well inside the EUR 3M per-signing budget.
title_plan: Defensive crisis: conceding 2.0 goals per game (rank 14th) against a top-sides average of 0.67 is the single biggest gap. The goalkeeper's pass accuracy sits at 64.93% versus contenders' 76.64%, compounding pressure on a back line where centre-back duel-win rate is only 53.97% against the top sides' 64.03%.

Attacking mid is a rated weakness (score 35/100): key passes at 0.65 per game are 12th-percentile, successful dribbles at 0.16 per game are 6th-percentile. A 27-year-old from the Peruvian Primera División (market value EUR 800k) produces 3.03 key passes and 0.56 assists per 90 — both at the 97th percentile.

Wingers score 50/100 but generate 0.0 goals per game against a top-sides average of 0.31. Combining a stronger attacking mid with the existing xG of 1.68 per game (5th in the league) should convert more of those chances without requiring wholesale forward investment.
money_plan: EUR 13M of squad value sits on expiring contracts. Prioritise extending the 26-year-old winger (market value EUR 3.5M, 2 months left, playing 92% of the minutes share) immediately — losing him on a free is the single biggest financial risk on the books.

Sell four underperforming assets now: an attacking mid aged 29 outperformed by 76% of league regulars (market value EUR 2M), plus three bench players each valued at EUR 1.2M with minute shares of 7–23%. Combined market value: EUR 5.6M — recyclable budget for the next window.

All three attacking-mid targets cost between EUR 750k and EUR 1M in market value against a EUR 3M per-signing budget, saving EUR 2.675M–EUR 2.925M versus comparable top-side profiles. The 20-year-old from the South African Premier League (EUR 750k) offers the best cost-to-impact ratio at the 91st percentile on key stats.
